<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Islamic terrorism in Europe]]
**Across [[Denmark]], [[Police of Denmark|police]] arrest twenty [[Islamist]]s who were planning attacks. Bomb materials were found in some of the houses during the [[police raid|raids]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/dec/11/islamist-terrorism-suspects-arrested-in-raids-across-denmark (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2019 Bagram Airfield attack]]
**[[Taliban]] forces assaulted a [[United States Air Force|United States]] [[air base]] in [[Afghanistan]] amidst [[Afghan peace process|peace talks]] between the two parties. The attackers killed two civilians and injured another 80 people using two [[car bomb]]s and guns. The attackers were successfully repelled by a [[NATO]] mission present at the base along with support from US fighter aircraft. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/12/11/world/asia/Afghanistan-bagram-airfield-attack.html (''The New York Times'')][https://www.militarytimes.com/flashpoints/2019/12/11/airstrikes-called-in-as-taliban-attempt-to-breach-bagram-air-base/ (Military Times)]
*[[2019 Inates attack]]
**At least 71 people were killed after [[terrorist]]s stormed a [[military base]] in [[Inates]], [[Niger]]. The attack was carried out by suspected [[Islamic State in the Greater Sahara]] militants. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-50744649 (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-niger-security/jihadists-kill-71-soldiers-in-mass-attack-niger-military-idUSKBN1YF2DF?il=0 (Reuters)]
*At least three patients were killed and several other people were injured during a protest outside the [[Punjab Institute of Cardiology]], [[Lahore]], [[Pakistan]]. It was staged by the lawyers against a mocking [[viral video]] from doctors. The mob also attacked at the provincial information minister of [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]] [[Fayyaz ul Hassan Chohan]]. The Young Doctors Association of Pakistan reports death of 12 patients. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1521675 (Dawn)] [https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2019/12/11/at-least-four-dead-as-lawyers-attack-pic/ (Pakistan Today)] 

;Business and economy
*Shares from [[Saudi Aramco]] begin trading on the [[Tadawul|Riyadh stock exchange]], where it surged to the maximum limit of 10% above its [[Initial public offering|IPO]] price. This increased the company's worth to [[U.S. dollar|US$]]1.88 trillion, making it the [[List of public corporations by market capitalization|most valuable publicly-traded company]] in the world. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-saudi-aramco-ipo-markets/vindication-saudi-arabia-hails-10-debut-jump-in-aramco-shares-idUSKBN1YF0LC (Reuters)]
*The [[World Trade Organization]]'s [[Dispute settlement in the World Trade Organization#WTO Appellate Body|Appellate Body]] ceases functioning. The tenure of two of its three remaining judges expires after the [[United States]] blocked the appointment of new judges and the quorum needed for a valid appeals ruling cannot be reached anymore. [https://www.scmp.com/economy/china-economy/article/3041490/china-blames-us-wtos-appeal-court-comes-halt-sparking-new (''SCMP'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2019–20 Australian bushfire season]], [[Physical impacts of climate change]], [[Individual and political action on climate change]]
**Around 7,500 people in [[Sydney]], [[New South Wales]], [[Australia]], stage a protest against [[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]]'s lack of acknowledgement towards an ongoing [[bushfire]] caused by [[drought]] and [[climate change]]. [https://www.news.com.au/technology/environment/climate-change/pressure-mounts-on-scott-morrison-to-act-on-climate-change-as-bushfire-crisis-continues/news-story/0d129ed6942484e8c0e986326832da35 (news.com.au)]

;Law and crime
*During her first speech before the [[International Court of Justice]] at [[The Hague]], [[Myanmar]]'s leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] denies all charges of [[genocide]], blames separatists and says the accusations are "misleading". [https://www.euronews.com/2019/12/10/aung-san-suu-kyi-at-the-icj-for-myanmar-genocide-trial (Euronews)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-rohingya-world-court/suu-kyi-tell-u-n-s-top-court-charge-of-rohingya-genocide-is-misleading-idUSKBN1YF06P (Reuters)]
*The [[Rajya Sabha]] of [[India]] votes 125 to 105 to pass [[The Citizenship (Amendment) Bill, 2019|a controversial amendment]] to the [[Indian nationality law]] that would expedite citizenship for [[religious minorities in India|religious minorities]] from [[Bangladesh]], [[Pakistan]], and [[Afghanistan]]. As the bill omits [[Islam in South Asia|Muslims]], critics say it's discriminatory and violates the secular nature of the [[Constitution of India|Constitution]]. Massive protests break out in the state of [[Assam]] in response. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-50739593 (BBC News)] 

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Bougainvillean independence referendum]]
**Voters in [[Autonomous Region of Bougainville|Bougainville]] vote overwhelmingly for independence from [[Papua New Guinea]]. However, the [[Papua New Guinea government]] will have the final say on accepting it or not. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-50739203 (BBC News)]
